searches.note: Twenty two searches of a share of twenty eight; six left unspent for the run's shared allowance. Most were read as summaries, several restricted to the VDP's or a house's own domain. Writers' own sites that came up were read and never cited. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the dates, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making, the window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.

The finding that matters most: the Aldinger site figures belonged to the VDP's other page, Gips, not Gips Marienglas; and three story beats (a teacher of 1858 at Fellbach, Dautel's takeover of 2013, Kreation of 1990) rested on nothing found and were cut or corrected.

tested: The Ruthe on the VDP's own pages: first named 1385, south facing, partly terraced, 20 to 40 per cent, 246 to 307 metres, Gipskeuper with coloured marl above, sheltered by the Siegelsberg, a monopole of the house. Kept, with the height and soil added.

The palace of 1702 over the moats, its vaulted cellars, the castle of the thirteenth century, the count's rank of 1726 and the Lemberger tradition: the house's own pages (Lemberger told there as a reputation, as the record does); 1702 and 1726 also in Wikipedia's Schwaigern and County of Neipperg articles.
Wilhelm Reinhard (1684 to 1774), count from 1726; the county taken into Württemberg in 1806: Wikipedia's county article and its succession list.
Adam Albert (8 April 1775 to 22 February 1829), Austrian general, grandson of Wilhelm Reinhard, morganatic marriage to Marie Louise in 1821: Wikipedia and Britannica.
1971: the purchase of Canon-La-Gaffelière and La Mondotte, with Clos de l'Oratoire and Peyreau months later, by the family's own Bordeaux site and trade pages. Kept, buyer unnamed.

The wine: Falstaff lists Schwaigern Ruthe Lemberger GG across vintages with 18 months in barrique; the house's lists give the Ruthe and Schlossberg Rieslings as dry Qualitätswein, so the others entry was corrected.

tested: 1492 and Bentz der Aldinger: the VDP's estate page and the house's own page agree; told as the family's account.

Gips Marienglas: the VDP lists GIPS MARIENGLAS as a Grosse Lage (5.66 hectares classified) and has a separate page GIPS whose figures (S to SW, 240 to 320 metres, 10 to 30 per cent, 6.63 hectares) the author had used; the figures were cut.

The house's page: Gips bought in 1973, replanted from 1974, named for gypsum quarried there some two centuries ago, its flagship site (Flaggschifflage), held alone; a cooperage turned into a wine estate in 1955 (not added).
The making: the house's sheet of 2024 gives wild yeast fermentation in wooden casks and ten months on the lees; that of 2018 a large wooden cask.
The swap: Falstaff lists the Lämmler Lemberger GG across many vintages; only a writer's wiki calls it the flagship, and the house calls the Gips its flagship site.

swaps.proposed: Change the wine from Untertürkheimer Gips Marienglas Riesling GG to Fellbacher Lämmler Lemberger GG, keeping the key and the producer.
swaps.why: The house's own page calls the Gips its flagship site (Flaggschifflage) and holds it alone; only a writer's wiki calls the Lämmler Lemberger the flagship, and Falstaff merely lists both GGs across vintages. Neither the house nor two sources lead with the Lämmler Lemberger, so the merge read's condition for a swap is not met. The Lämmler Lemberger stays in others.
